findings.action: Decode Markdown destinations before testing the association namespace and extension, or report unsupported forms as unknown. The reader does not decode URL escapes or Markdown character references; it also truncates numeric character references at '#'. Thus '[decision](../adr/decision%2Emd)', '[decision](../adr/decision.md)' and '[decision](../%61dr/decision.md)' all name the canonical decision.md but are silently skipped at lines 174-175. Equivalent backlinks to pair.md are skipped at lines 245-246. A read-only reproduction using the extracted production regex and namespace predicates confirmed associations=[] and diagnostics=[] for all six forward/backward cases. With two resolved members and no other association, evaluateCloseoutReview therefore returns Known=true and Required=false, violating R3. Normalize supported destination escapes before containment checks, or fail closed, and cover both association directions.
Complete existing spec follow-up F6 with context-aware Markdown parsing while retaining fail-closed behavior for unsupported or unresolved local associations.
findings.rationale: Existing spec follow-up F6 remains applicable: links shown in code or comments count as associations, and destinations containing parentheses return unknown even when a complete Markdown parser could resolve them. This can demand unnecessary review, but does not grant an exemption. Inspection and the passing TestCloseoutReviewPolicyRoundTwelve/RoundFourteen regressions confirm the conservative behavior; accept this limited over-enforcement risk.
